turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip was being unreasonable, and Nikhil would not stand idly by while his tenantry was oppressed, so he demanded that Sandip desist from his oppressive ways immediately, and leave his territory once and for all.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ha! Nikhil was now threatening him with his tenantry's complaints? How quaint, how amusing. As if they wouldn't sell their souls to the highest bidder, just like their masters.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's levity is an insult, and it will not be tolerated. He must leave now, and take his oppression with him.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What's the great Nikhil's game now? Is he trying to protect his precious tenantry or just his precious pride?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: It is not a matter of pride, Sandip, but of duty. As a zamindar, it is his obligation to protect his tenantry.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Nikhil's duty, ha! As if anyone actually believes in that nonsense anymore. Besides, what's there to protect? His precious tenantry or his own precious ego?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's condescending attitude is a weakness, and it will be his undoing. He would do well to listen to reason for once.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: What a sanctimonious speech, Nikhil, full of empty virtue-signaling. He's as worried about his precious tenantry as a cat is about its whiskers.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's words are a poor reflection on his character, and it is time he took the threats seriously.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was intrigued, he asked Bimala, have you heard the latest, it seems Nikhil's got a new hobby - pretending to be the zamindar's conscience.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's eyes narrowed slightly as she observed, Nikhil's concerns seemed to be falling on deaf ears, Sandip, and she couldn't help but wonder why Sandip was being so obstinate.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip was furious, he exclaimed, if Nikhil thought a few empty threats from the Mussulmans would drive them out of their own land.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's negligence will only embolden the Mussulmans to make good on their threats, and he would do well to remember the lessons of the past.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip's eyes narrowed as he gazed at Bimala, his voice low and measured, 'You see the concern in Nikhil's eyes, it's almost... endearing, like a misplaced sense of duty.'

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala seemed to think that Nikhil's warnings were not just empty threats, but a genuine concern for the estate's well-being, and that it would be prudent to take them seriously, especially considering Sandip's involvement.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Sandip's recklessness will be his downfall, mark his words, for a zamindar's primary duty is to protect his estate and its people, not to indulge in foolish bravado.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala's words dripped with caution, as she warned Sandip and Nikhil that it would be unwise to underestimate Nikhil's words, considering the recent disturbances in the region.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip chuckled, his eyes glinting with amusement, 'Oh, Nikhil's words are as dry as the winter air, full of warnings and no wine to ease the sting.'

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: His estate's safety is paramount, and Nikhil would not be ignored, for a zamindar's word is not to be taken lightly, especially when it comes to matters of security.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip rolled his eyes, a wry smile playing on his lips, 'Pooh, Nikhil's warnings are as plentiful as the stars in the sky, but as useful as a pinch of salt in the winter rains, what a waste of breath.'

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
